- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +3%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +2% above recent peak for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 0.5–1% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underestimates true price in early forecast horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish — adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% for short-term (1–3 day) forecasts.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (or vice versa) within 3–5 days, model lags; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often overestimates mean price; apply 1–3% downward correction if sentiment is mixed or bearish in last 5–7 days.
- If sentiment is consistently high (≥0.8) and price is rising, model may overfit trend; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5–7 days to avoid overextension.
